canonical_statement: MERCURI-2 tested whether dapagliflozin initiated 1 day before elective cardiac surgery reduces KDIGO acute kidney injury within 7 postoperative days compared with placebo.
MERCURI-2 was an investigator-initiated, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled superiority trial conducted at 7 hospitals in the Netherlands.
Eligible participants were adults aged 18 years or older scheduled for elective cardiac surgery.

Key exclusions were type 1 diabetes; selected insulin-treated type 2 diabetes with BMI below 25; eGFR below 20 mL/min/1.73 m2; prior diabetic ketoacidosis; systolic blood pressure below 100 mm Hg; current SGLT2 inhibitor treatment; SGLT2 inhibitor allergy; and pregnancy, breastfeeding, or inadequate contraception when applicable.

population.label: MERCURI-2 exclusion criteria
exclusion_criteria: Type 2 diabetes with BMI below 25 using multiple daily insulin injections
Systolic blood pressure below 100 mm Hg at enrollment evaluation
Known or suspected SGLT2 inhibitor allergy
Pregnancy, breastfeeding, intent to become pregnant, or inadequate contraception when applicable

canonical_statement: Randomization used a 1:1 ratio with computer-generated block sizes of 4, 6, and 8, stratified by sex, type 2 diabetes, and study site; allocation was visible only to trial pharmacists.
Participants assigned to dapagliflozin received 10 mg orally once daily for 4 doses: the evening before surgery, the morning of surgery, postoperative day 1, and postoperative day 2.

canonical_statement: Participants assigned to placebo received matching oral placebo on the same 4-dose perioperative schedule.

canonical_statement: The primary outcome was KDIGO acute kidney injury within 7 days after surgery, defined by creatinine or urine-output criteria.

outcome.definition: KDIGO AKI: serum creatinine increase of at least 0.3 mg/dL within 48 hours, at least 1.5 times baseline within 7 days, or urine output below 0.5 mL/kg/h for 6 to 12 hours.
outcome.measurement_method: Daily serum creatinine while hospitalized and hourly urine output while urinary catheter present

canonical_statement: Stage 3 AKI was a prespecified secondary outcome using KDIGO stage 3 criteria.

outcome.definition: Kidney replacement therapy, serum creatinine at least 4.0 mg/dL or at least 3 times baseline within 7 days, urine output below 0.3 mL/kg/h for 24 hours, or anuria for more than 12 hours.

canonical_statement: The primary analysis compared randomized groups without imputation for missing data; dichotomous outcomes were reported with risk differences and relative risks with 95% confidence intervals, and the primary outcome was also adjusted for sex by logistic regression.
The planned sample size was 784 participants, based on an assumed 22% placebo AKI incidence, expected relative risk of 0.64, 80% power, and a two-sided alpha of 0.05.
The trial randomized 784 participants, 392 per group; median age was 68 years, 76% were male, 97% were White, 12% had type 2 diabetes, and 6% had heart failure.

canonical_statement: Protocol adherence was high: 344 of 392 dapagliflozin participants and 339 of 392 placebo participants took all 4 study tablets.
Dapagliflozin reduced 7-day KDIGO AKI compared with placebo: 111 of 392 participants (28%) versus 205 of 392 (52%), relative risk 0.54 (95% CI 0.45 to 0.65; P<.001).

canonical_statement: The authors concluded that 4 doses of dapagliflozin beginning the day before elective cardiac surgery reduced AKI incidence during the 7-day postoperative period.
The primary outcome covered only 7 days, and no statistically significant between-group differences were found in secondary clinical outcomes.
The trial was not powered to detect differences in stage 3 AKI or MAKE30.

Generalizability was limited by a study population that was 97% White and 76% male, excluded current SGLT2 inhibitor users, and contained relatively few participants with type 2 diabetes, heart failure, or chronic kidney disease.
Results were limited to elective cardiac surgery, were not adjusted for multiplicity across secondary outcomes, and may not generalize to other SGLT2 inhibitors.
The prespecified primary analysis did not adjust for all randomization stratification factors; post hoc analyses repeated the primary outcome adjusting for sex, type 2 diabetes, and site.

The study did not collect the proportion of participants lacking a creatinine measurement on the day before surgery, so the time between baseline creatinine measurement and surgery could not be analyzed.

The trial was supported by the Netherlands Organization for Health Research and Development, and the article states that funders had no role in study design, conduct, analysis, interpretation, manuscript preparation, or publication decision.
